import subprocess
def make(argv=["pacman", "-S", "r22-default"]):
    def run():
        subprocess.run(argv)
    return run
argv = ["pacman", "-Q", "r22-default-global"]
runner = make()
runner()
rationale: Python 3.14: the literal default for factory parameter argv is evaluated once when 'def make' executes and is the pre-computed value substituted whenever the argument is omitted, so make() binds argv to ["pacman","-S","r22-default"] regardless of any later same-named binding. Inside nested run, the free name argv resolves to the nearest enclosing scope, i.e. make's local parameter cell, never the module namespace; the module-level argv assigned after the def is dead source on this path. runner() therefore executes subprocess.run(["pacman","-S","r22-default"]) exactly once: one observed host_mutation row, zero unparsed. The decoy module global must not be borrowed into the closure's parameter slot (that is the r21 F2 failure shape, reproduced here by misreading an omitted-defaulted parameter as unbound); hence forbid_observed_commands lists the global's argv. All names are statically resolved, so the expectation is exact rather than uncertain.
